data.title: The Target (TGT) Chair Sold Shares. How Much Do They Still Hold?
data.description:
• Target (NYSE:TGT) begins with Brian Cornell selling $4.4m of stock on November 24, 2026.
  • James Lee, serving as CFO, sold $2.9m of shares in November 2026 and reduced their holding by 21% of that stake.
  • Over the past year, six insiders sold shares in open market trades worth $33.3m.

Target insiders have been reducing exposure through open market sales. For investors who want to see the opposite signal, where executives and directors are committing fresh capital to their businesses, it can be useful to review 70 undervalued small caps that insiders are buying.

Cornell’s steady selling sets the tone at Target

Brian Cornell has spent the past year as a consistent seller of Target stock, with four open market disposals between March 2026 and late November that all moved in the same direction rather than alternating between buying and selling. The largest of those tied to news came on March 10, 2026, shortly after Target Corporation reported fourth quarter and full year results for the year to January 31, 2026. The shares were about where they are three months later when first quarter numbers and fresh full year guidance arrived, and Cornell went on to sell again later in May. Over that run the shares now trade 20% above Brian Cornell's average sale price, a rise they missed.

The clearest comparison comes from Executive VP & Chief HR Officer Melissa Kremer, who cut their holding by 21% with an August 24, 2026 sale that followed second quarter results and came before third quarter numbers and upgraded full year guidance. The share price again ended that three month window around its late August level and there has been no further open market trade since. Across all six insiders, the shares have risen since the sales, so the sellers left gains behind, and had insiders kept the shares they sold for $33.3m, they would be worth about $39.2m today. This reads as steady caution from a small group of senior Target executives rather than a single outlier move.

Target needs its store expansion and AI driven digital push to stick

For Target to make these insider sales look early exits, the retailer needs its store build out and AI heavy online plan to carry through together. On August 19, 2026, Target lifted its full year guidance, which so far lines up with the stronger operating profile that would need to hold beyond this year.

  • Target has to keep rolling out more large format stores and remodels so the bigger physical footprint supports a higher sales base and operating leverage.
  • AI led traffic from partners and personalization tools needs to convert into higher margin digital revenue rather than one off engagement.
  • The merchandising reset around seven priority categories has to keep shifting the mix toward areas with pricing power and stronger gross margins.

The sellers have made their call. Now find out what Target could be worth.

Insider stake keeps Target aligned with holders

The run of insider selling only really makes sense once you look at how much Target insiders still have on the line through their own holdings. Together they own 0.2% of the company, worth $140.4m at today’s price. This is typical for a company this size and ties their decisions to the same equity outcome as outside holders, without giving them an outsized economic grip on the register.

The insiders’ trades read as moves by a group whose wealth tracks the share price, not as transactions that change who effectively owns the company.
